intel.t: He runs as an independent minded Democrat leading from the center, focused on pocketbook costs, and says there is room for Trump voters in his campaign.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Marshall's camp ties him to Schumer and national Democrats and attacks his handling of a 2005 church camp report, calling him unfit; Hamilton says the inquiry was inconclusive and he should have called police.
Unaffiliated voters, about 29 percent of Kansas registrants; Emerson in September had him up 42 to 27 among independents and 45 to 43 overall.
The Kansas Livestock Association declined to endorse Marshall this cycle and farmers are angry over tariffs and diesel, though many still distrust Democrats on farming.
Cook moved the race to Toss Up on October 6, 2026, and Trump rallied near Wichita for Marshall on October 19.
He outraised Marshall nearly three to one through September 30, but Marshall's side had nearly ten times the ad reservations as of October 2.

bottom: Hamilton is a first time candidate and the founding pastor of the Church of the Resurrection in Leawood, which a Kansas Reflector headline of July 22, 2026 calls the nation's largest Methodist church. He entered the race on April 30, 2026 and became one of the strongest Democratic fundraisers in the Senate map. A VoteLog compilation of FEC data shows $13,533,711 raised through September 30, 2026, of which $12,231,674 came from individuals and only $195,000 from PACs, https://votelog.org/investigations/kansas-senate-general-money. CQ Roll Call reported another $5.6 million from October 1 to 14, https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/oct/23/senate-democratic-candidates-keep-the-cash-flowing/.

**Small and in-state donors.** His first four days brought $1.01 million from 6,700 donors, about 70 percent from Kansas, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/05/04/democrat-running-for-u-s-senate-receives-1-million-in-donations-in-campaigns-first-week/.

**Democratic Senate super PACs.** Groups counted as benefiting Hamilton include People Over Politics Action Fund at $9,657,045, WinSenate at $8,139,349 and Lower Costs Now at $2,933,659. WinSenate and Lower Costs Now are funded largely by SMP. Total outside money benefiting him was $27,771,284 through October 22, 2026, against $18,359,813 benefiting Marshall, per VoteLog.

intel.t: Keep Trump's agenda going and keep the Senate Republican; he told voters control of the Senate goes through Kansas.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Tariffs, diesel prices from the Iran war and the beef import waiver hit farmers, and the patient lawsuits; Trump's Kansas approval was 40 percent in a September Emerson poll.
Trump aligned Republicans, who outnumber Democrats about 900,000 to 500,000 in registration; he drew more than 6,000 to a Trump rally near Wichita on October 19.
The Kansas Livestock Association declined to endorse him for the first time since 2016.
Outraised about three to one by Hamilton through September 30, but SLF, Main Street Fund, AFP Action and Club for Growth Action are covering the gap.

bottom: Marshall is a physician turned congressman who sits on the Agriculture, Finance, HELP and Budget committees. His own campaign is being outraised by a first time candidate, so the national Republican super PAC network carries his race. VoteLog shows his campaign at $4,809,692 raised, $5,592,623 spent and $922,088 cash through September 30, 2026, against Hamilton's $13,533,711 raised, https://votelog.org/investigations/kansas-senate-general-money. Time, relaying AdImpact, says nearly ten times as much ad money was reserved for Marshall as for Hamilton as of October 2, https://time.com/article/2026/10/07/why-kansas-has-emerged-as-a-new-battleground-state-and-why-it-matters/.
Interests with money and a live decision:

**Party and leadership.** Senate Leadership Fund leads outside spending for him at $6,286,982 and, per Time, reserved $8.2 million for Kansas. SLF's cycle funders include Elon Musk at $168 million and Miriam Adelson at $30 million.

**Koch and Club for Growth network.** AFP Action at $2,598,895 and Club for Growth Action at $2,456,460 back him. Their top cycle funders are Koch Inc. at $30 million and Jeff Yass at $16.5 million. The ask is tax and regulatory policy that runs through Finance and Budget, where he sits.

D.t: Adam Hamilton leads by 0.7 in the forecast and wins 53% of simulations. The cushion is about 8,248 votes; a one point swing is about 5,728 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +6.8 and D +8.4. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +2.2. Your best recent poll is Emerson College / Nexstar at D +2.8; your worst is RedBox Research (D) at R +2.1. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Johnson, a projected net 94,399 votes; Douglas, a projected net 30,484 votes; Wyandotte, a projected net 21,289 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sedgwick, D +2.7, 15.9% of the vote; Leavenworth, R +4.7, 2.7% of the vote; Crawford, R +6.5, 1.2% of the vote; Harvey, R +5.7, 1.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Adam Hamilton runs furthest behind in Pottawatomie, Butler, McPherson. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 88% of voters, 46 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.41 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 48 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.51 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 56 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.88 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Adam Hamilton: Immigration voters 13 to 84, Small counties 30 to 67, Voters who can afford daily costs 36 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.7M cash against $922K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 45% of the 274,728 ballots in Kansas so far, against 41% for the other party. That is 11.4 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

media.what: Breaking Points ran a 'GOP Panic Over Kansas' segment on Senate Leadership Fund spending about $14 million to rescue Sen. Roger Marshall.
Hosted Rich Baris, who said Kansas, Nebraska, Montana, Texas and Ohio could all be Democratic openings.
Named Kansas among toss up Senate races, with polling showing a tie or Democrats up a few points.
Said Democrats will fall short in Kansas but it is a race.
Said the GOP moving money to defend Roger Marshall in Kansas was not on anyone's bingo card.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Kansas Senate from Likely R to Lean R.
Inside Elections moved the Kansas Senate race between Roger Marshall and Adam Hamilton from Likely Republican to Tilt Republican.
On Anderson Cooper 360 he said polling in the Kansas Senate race is tied and listed it among the races that could hand Democrats a majority.
Interviewed Sen. Roger Marshall in Wichita for Fox News Digital, where Marshall said that if Republicans lose Kansas he does not see how they keep the Senate.
Interviewed Democrat Adam Hamilton on his campaign bus for Hopium Chronicles, where Hamilton said early voting looks really strong and slammed Roger Marshall for skipping town halls.
On the RealClearPolitics podcast he said many Kansans remain angry the Epstein files are unreleased, as an Epstein themed ad targets Roger Marshall in a race within one point.
